\tutentry{FERMENTATION}{tutorials/plant/ChemicalPlantTutorial/FERMENTATION}
\begin{tutnarrative}
/ system/flowsheetDict (SECTOR -- COMPOSITE with INTERNAL RECYCLE)

Continuous fermentation side-loop of the sugar plant: a slip-stream of fresh juice (Must) is hydrolysed + fermented into ethanol + CO2, the Flash splits the volatiles (EthanolVapour product) from the liquid bottoms, and a Splitter recycles 80 \% of the bottoms back to the Mixer so unconverted sucrose gets another shot. Pedagogical purpose:

1. Reaction (Arrhenius first-order in sucrose). 2. Vapour-liquid flash for separation. 3. Tear-stream RECYCLE that the Wegstein/Newton outer loop must iterate to a fixed point.

Must    [Mixer]  MixedFeed   [Fermentor]  FermOut   [Flash]   EthanolVapour           Liquid       Recycle     [Splitter]                     

Tear stream: Recycle (Splitter output $\to$ Mixer input).

\end{tutnarrative}

\clearpage
\tutentry{MAIN}{tutorials/plant/ChemicalPlantTutorial/MAIN}
\begin{tutnarrative}
ChemicalPlantTutorial / MAIN / system/flowsheetDict (SECTOR -- COMPOSITE)

THE MAIN SECTOR: the plant-level operations that belong to no specialised sector. Here that is one unit, the JuiceSplitter, which takes the single RawJuice header and splits it 2/3 to CONCENTRATION and 1/3 to FERMENTATION.

WHY A LEVEL FOR ONE UNIT (2026-09-05, amended 2026-09-07). Until 09-05 the JuiceSplitter sat at the plant root beside the sectors -- a PascalCase unit folder among CAPS folders, breaking the convention this case's own header declares. The rule the plant now teaches: a folder in CAPS is always a level of the plant's geography, and a plant-level unit lives in MAIN/. MAIN/ is THE DOMAIN'S OWN LEVEL, not a sector like the others (the 2026-09-07 amendment), which is why the plant's own inlets and every stream crossing two sectors live there too -- a stream's file goes at the lowest level whose subtree contains every endpoint of it. The STATE views repeat the whole geography: 0/ and converged/ both carry MAIN, CONCENTRATION, DRYING, FERMENTATION. A DERIVATIVE view carries only what it has something to say about -- design/ has no MAIN/, because a splitter realises no sized item -- and that absence is a fact, not a gap to fill. Flat cases are untouched: a case with no sectors has no MAIN either (its units ARE the plant).

\end{tutnarrative}

\tutwhat{ACETIC ACID FROM CO + METHANOL -- a basic Gibbs-reactor tutorial. One gibbsReactor with the six species of the carbonylation chemistry (CO, methanol, acetic acid, dimethyl ether, methyl acetate, water) at 460 K and 30 bar, detuned by a 10 K approach to equilibrium. Thermodynamic ceiling only: no catalyst, no rate law.}
\begin{tutnarrative}
acetic acid from CO + methanol.

CO + CH3OH $\to$ CH3COOH (the carbonylation) 2 CH3OH <$\to$ CH3OCH3 + H2O (dimethyl ether) CH3OH + CH3COOH <$\to$ CH3COOCH3 + H2O (methyl acetate)

The reactor is a `gibbsReactor`: it is given the SPECIES and their atoms, never the reactions above. It finds the composition that minimises the Gibbs energy at 460 K and 30 bar, so every pathway the six species allow is open at once. `temperatureApproach 10` then detunes it: the engine evaluates the REACTION equilibrium 10 K away from the physical T (it reads the sign from the thermicity of this feed), so the outlet is 10 K short of equilibrium.

feed (CO + methanol) -$\to$ [reactor] -$\to$ gas -$\to$ liquid

TOPOLOGY ONLY. Stream state lives on disk in 0/, one file per stream.

\end{tutnarrative}
\tutreadme{A basic tutorial: ONE gibbsReactor, six species, a 10 K approach to equilibrium. It answers a single question --- $\ast$what does thermodynamics alone allow when CO and methanol meet at 460 K and 30 bar?$\ast$ --- and says nothing about how fast, or with what catalyst, it gets there.}
\tutreadme{The flowsheet never states these reactions. system/flowsheetDict lists the six species with their atoms (C, H, O) and the reactor minimises the Gibbs energy under the atom balances, so every pathway the six species allow is open at once. Species left out are pathways closed by decision: no CO2, H2, CH4, formaldehyde or iodides.}
\tutreadme{The feed is declared phase gas; at the reactor temperature on purpose: a stream at 300 K with CO and methanol together has no honest single phase, and the energy report refuses to price it (found while writing this case).}
\tutreadme{The lesson is that the by-products vanish. Carbonylation is so favourable (K \textasciitilde{} 2e5 bar\textasciicircum{}-1 at 470 K, from the formation data) that methanol is used up; methyl acetate and water exist only as the trace left in equilibrium with it, and DME is smaller still. In the real plant they are $\ast$intermediates$\ast$ whose level is set by kinetics and by the catalyst system, not by this equilibrium. A Gibbs reactor gives the ceiling, not the selectivity.}
\tutreadme{Hand check (order of magnitude, ideal gas, 470 K): dG(carbonylation) \textasciitilde{} -48 kJ/mol gives y\_MeOH \textasciitilde{} 1e-8 to 1e-7 with p\_CO \textasciitilde{} 24 bar and p\_AcOH \textasciitilde{} 6 bar; the engine's 4e-8 agrees. Methyl acetate then follows from K \textasciitilde{} 60 for the esterification, giving \textasciitilde{}7e-4, which also agrees.}
\tutreadme{temperatureApproach 10 is a MAGNITUDE. The engine reads the thermicity of this feed's transformation (exothermic, dH = -66 437 kJ per kmol of feed), assigns the sign, and evaluates the reaction equilibrium at T + 10 K = 470 K, announcing it. Compared with temperatureApproach 0:}

\tutwhat{ACETIC ACID FROM CO + METHANOL, rung 2 -- the plant around the Gibbs reactor of aceticAcid01: UNIFAC liquid instead of ideal, the reactor gas condensed, the CO recycled against a purge, a degasser, a lights column taking the light by-products (methyl acetate / water / methanol / dimethyl ether) overhead as a declared plant outlet, acetic acid as the bottoms product. One recycle (CO). Still a thermodynamic ceiling: no catalyst, no rate law.}
\begin{tutnarrative}
acetic acid from CO + methanol, with its plant. A BASE CASE: it runs, it is NOT optimised, and every number a student would tune is a plain key below (see README section 4).

freshMethanol $\to$ [methanolTank] $\to$ [methanolPump] $\to$ methanolToProcess 1 atm 14 days to 30 bar | +-------------------------------------------------------+

+---------------+ (freshCO arrives by pipeline, not stored) freshCO --------+-$\to$ [M1] -$\to$ [preheater] -$\to$ [reactor] ----$\to$ liquid ---+ coRecycle ------+ \textasciicircum{} 460 K gibbsReactor | | | 460 K, 30 bar, v | | approach 10 gas | | | | | [condenser] | | 330 K, 30 bar| | | | | | coGas condensate | | | | | [purgeSplit] +-[M2] | | | | | purge coRecycle v +--------------------------------------+ [letdown valve]

[lightsColumn] | | lightsOut acidProduct

[acidTank] -$\to$ acidShipped

ONE recycle: CO, against a 5 \% purge. The light by-products leave through the lights column's distillate (a declared outlet, not recycled -- a second recycle was built first and cost 7 min 25 s a run for a stream that is 94 \% acetic acid). The reactor is the one of aceticAcid01\_gibbsReactor.

THE TANKS (DEV.md 4c C87). The methanol is BOUGHT and held in a feed tank before the process takes it; the acid is COOLED and held in a product tank between shipments. Both tanks are `storageTank` units: the outlet IS the inlet (same F, z, T, P), so they move no process number -- what they add is the holdup the plant's working capital rests on, and the equipment the plot plan and an economic analysis must carry. They are SIZED in system/postDict, by a `storage` entry that LINKS each unit (`unit methanolTank;`) and reads its residence time, fill fraction and inlet from it: the stock is declared ONCE, here. CO is NOT stored: it arrives by pipeline at the plant pressure, as a gas no atmospheric tank holds.

\end{tutnarrative}
\tutreadme{Rung 2 after aceticAcid01\_gibbsReactor. The same Gibbs reactor, now inside a plant: a methanol feed tank and its pump, a condenser, a CO recycle against a purge, a degasser, a lights column, a product cooler and an acetic acid product tank. It runs (32 s), it converges, and it is deliberately NOT optimised --- every number a student would tune is a plain key in system/flowsheetDict. The optimisation is the exercise.}
\tutreadme{The case is sealed: everything it reads is in its own constant/.}
\tutreadme{One recycle (CO), closed with Wegstein in 46 iterations. A second recycle (the lights column's distillate back to the reactor) was built first and abandoned: it cost 7 min 25 s a run, and the stream it recycled is 94 \% acetic acid. lightsOut is a declared plant outlet.}
\tutreadme{Two tanks and a product cooler (added 2026-10-18, DEV.md 4c C87): the methanol the plant buys is held in methanolTank before the process takes it, and the acid it makes is cooled in acidCooler and held in acidTank between shipments. The tanks are storageTank units: the outlet IS the inlet, so they move no process number; what they add is the inventory and the equipment (section 8). The cooler is a phaseChanger against the plant's cooling water: the acid leaves the column at its bubble point at 1.5 bar, about 404 K -- 13 K above its normal boiling point (391.05 K) -- and an atmospheric tank cannot hold a liquid hotter than it boils. The CO is not stored: it arrives by pipeline at the plant pressure.}
\tutreadme{$\ast$ Reactor: the Gibbs reactor of rung 1 --- equilibrium at 460 K, 30 bar, 10 K approach. No catalyst, no rate. Its liquid is ideal by construction (elementPotential: gas plus one ideal condensable); the 10 K barely moves the main product (see rung 1). $\ast$ Separations: UNIFAC, which is predictive --- the catalogue has no regressed pair for most of this system. Every activity coefficient is an estimate from structure. $\ast$ Vapour: ideal gas. Acetic acid is largely dimerised in real vapour. The engine models that dimer only on its REACTIVE-equilibrium path (a vapourDimerisation block on the acid's gas-liquid chemistry record; see tutorials/steady/flash/flash12\_nh3\_acetic\_ethanol\_reactive and flash13); a gamma-phi package like this one (UNIFAC liquid, ideal-gas vapour) has no vapour-association fugacity model, so this case does not use it and the condenser and degasser splits are indicative. $\ast$ CO has no UNIFAC group, so it sits outside the activity model (approximations block, announced as a $\ast$substitution$\ast$ on every run). $\ast$ Battery limits: the methanol arrives as a liquid at 1 atm into its feed tank, and methanolPump (efficiency 0.65, assumed) lifts it to 30 bar. The CO arrives by pipeline, declared at 30 bar; no CO compressor is modelled. $\ast$ The pump's own energy balance is announced as FAILED on every run (dH 1.76 kW against 5.04 kW of shaft work, 35 \% = 1 - eta). It is the engine's, not the case's: the liquid enthalpy of this package carries no pressure term (measured here -- moving 0/freshMethanol from 30 bar to 1 atm left the plant's feed enthalpy unchanged to the last digit), so the 3.28 kW of useful work v$\cdot$dP the pump puts into the liquid is invisible to the energy report, and only its 1.76 kW of dissipation shows as a temperature rise. tutorials/steady/rotating/pump01\_water shows the same 65 \% gap. $\ast$ Data: dimethyl ether is reviewStatus interim with a Joback formation enthalpy (see rung 1); it is nil in every stream here. $\ast$ Antoine ranges are exceeded at 460 K (dozens of announcements per run) and the column prints [distillate] WARNING lines (47 in the base case): the distillate's bubble point does not converge because CO and dimethyl ether have no real saturation curve at those temperatures, so the distillate temperature is reported at the top tray. Neither changes a flow.}

\tutwhat{Acetone from 2-propanol: Luyben's Figure 1 closed, with the IPA recycle}
\begin{tutnarrative}
ACETONE FROM 2-PROPANOL, THE CLOSED FLOWSHEET

W. L. Luyben, "Design and Control of the Acetone Process via Dehydrogenation of 2-Propanol", Ind. Eng. Chem. Res. 50 (2011) 1206-1218, DOI 10.1021/ie901923a -- his Figure 1 (the Turton base case), end to end:

fresh feed + IPA recycle $\to$ vaporiser $\to$ reactor $\to$ separator $\to$ absorber (offgas washed) $\to$ C1 $\to$ acetone product $\to$ C2 $\to$ water product $\to$ IPA RECYCLE (tear)

This is the case the six preceding ones were built to make possible. Each of them isolates one unit on Luyben's OWN published inlet, so that whatever it gets wrong is that unit and its thermodynamics. Here nothing is published except the fresh feed: every internal stream is the plant's own answer, and the errors compose.

WHAT THIS CASE CLAIMS, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. It claims to be Luyben's TOPOLOGY and Luyben's EQUIPMENT SPECIFICATIONS solved on the thermodynamics Choupo actually has. It does NOT claim to reproduce his stream table -- the siblings measured, in advance, exactly why it cannot, and the gap between his table and this one is the deliverable rather than a defect to be closed:

acetone01: UNIFAC puts the IPA/water azeotrope at x 0.590 against his 0.673, and the lake-estimated isopropanol boils 4.5 K high. acetone04: UNIFAC INVENTS an acetone/water azeotrope at x 0.978 where his UNIQUAC has none -- 0.044 K deep, and decisive. acetone06: so C1 caps at 97.3 mol \% acetone against his 99.9 \% spec. acetone07: so C2's recycle caps at x\_IPA 0.580 against his 0.650, and 11.6 \% of the isopropanol entering it leaves in the water product.

Both column ceilings were WRITTEN DOWN BEFORE the columns existed and are pinned by check\_azeotrope\_ceiling. This case is where they stop being two separate findings and become one plant.

DEPARTURES FROM HIS FIGURE 1, each argued rather than absorbed

(a) NO HYDROGEN IN THE COLUMNS. His C1 has a partial condenser and a vent (0.0465 kmol/h, carrying 0.0130 kmol/h H2 and 0.0335 kmol/h acetone); Choupo's column has a total condenser and no vapour distillate. A permanent gas fed to a total condenser is asked to leave as a liquid, and the engine rightly refuses (hydrogen has no liquid heat capacity at 330 K). So the separator's LIQUID goes to C1 and the hydrogen leaves with the offgas, i.e. the columns are modelled downstream of his vent. Cost, stated: the 0.0335 kmol/h of acetone his vent loses is not lost here, which flatters this plant's acetone recovery by 0.10 \%.

(b) THE SEPARATOR DOES THE COOLING. An isothermal flash at 318 K computes the duty to bring its feed there, so this one unit stands for his HX1 plus his separator and its Q is directly comparable to his 0.8993 MW. A separate `heater` was tried in acetone03 and refused, correctly: Choupo's heater takes a DUTY and reports the temperature, because a heater with a specified outlet temperature is a design specification.

(c) THE SEPARATOR PRESSURE IS ARGUED, NOT FITTED. Luyben states 1.5 atm for the absorber gas, which is downstream; there is no compressor between reactor and separator and pressure only falls, so the separator sits at the reactor's 2.6 atm. acetone03 records the sweep that would have tempted a fitted value and why it was refused.

(d) THE ABSORBER'S SECOND OUTLET REJOINS C1's FEED, as in his Figure 1 (his F1 of 72.85 kmol/h is the flash liquid AFTER the absorber bottoms of 20.05 kmol/h rejoin it).

(e) NO VENT/PURGE ON THE RECYCLE LOOP. Luyben has none either -- the loop closes through C2's overhead and nothing else -- so this is his structure, not a simplification. It does mean any component that both enters and cannot leave would accumulate without bound; here water leaves in three places and isopropanol in two, so the loop is closed and bounded.

\end{tutnarrative}
\tutreadme{Acetone from 2-propanol: the flowsheet of W. L. Luyben, $\ast$Design and Control of the Acetone Process via Dehydrogenation of 2-Propanol$\ast$, Ind. Eng. Chem. Res. 50 (2011) 1206, his Figure 1 end to end --- fresh feed and isopropanol recycle into a mixer, a vaporiser to 389 K, a conversion reactor at 623 K and 90 \% per-pass conversion, a separator chilled to 318 K, an absorber washing the offgas with 20 kmol/h of water, a vent, and two columns: C1 (66 stages, feed 54, R 2.78) making the acetone product and C2 (19 stages, feed 16, R 0.849) returning the isopropanol. Nine units, one cycle, and the cycle is declared: system/solverDict cuts it at ipaRecycle and closes it with Wegstein.}
\tutreadme{Everything on the first path so far arrives here at once --- an equilibrium, a model choice, a many-stage unit, a method that has to be chosen, a reaction, a graph, a recycle. And one thing more, which is why this case is last.}
\tutreadme{It does not reproduce Luyben's stream table, and that is the deliverable. Seven sibling cases (acetone01 to acetone07) each measured ONE unit on Luyben's own published inlet $\ast$before$\ast$ this plant existed, so every difference below was predicted rather than discovered. Nothing was tuned to close a gap.}
\tutreadme{That first row is 85 \% of his acetone, and the case's own CLAUDE.md records the product at 0.9727 mole fraction acetone against his 0.999 spec.}
\tutreadme{1. The error has an address, and it was written down first. UNIFAC invents an acetone/water azeotrope at x 0.978 where Luyben's UNIQUAC has none (acetone04), which caps C1; UNIFAC also misplaces the real isopropanol/water azeotrope at x 0.590 against 0.673 (acetone01), which caps C2. Both ceilings were measured on isolated units before either column was built, and the golden shows them arriving: C2 x\_D\_LK is 0.499124702623, and a wetter recycle carries less isopropanol, which makes less acetone, which is the production figure in the table. A plant whose disagreement you can name unit by unit is worth more than one that agrees for reasons nobody checked. 2. Two thermodynamic worlds, and the boundary is priced. Handed the plant's global UNIFAC package the absorber REFUSES by name: it solves Kremser, Kremser reads Henry's law, and an activity model carries no answer it can use. So that unit alone carries an inline thermo \{\} block --- water the solvent on the pure-liquid rung, acetone the solute on the Henry rung --- declared where the model boundary is and announced when the run crosses it. The block is inline in system/flowsheetDict rather than in a file of its own for exactly that reason. The model-boundary ledger then prices the crossing independently and writes its verdict to reports/balances/energyBalance\_byUnit.csv: raw imbalance -11.2496 kW, declared boundary step 0.0000 kW, remaining -11.2496 kW, and in the report's own words $\ast$the step is NOT credited$\ast$. Read the report for it, not the expected file: that row is held by check\_model\_boundary\_ledger, and this case's golden carries no row kind that can read it. Changing the liquid activity model changes K-values, not the enthalpy datum, so there is nothing to credit at this boundary --- and the residual that remains belongs to the absorber's own lumped-Cp energy model, which the case's CLAUDE.md traces and does not excuse. 3. A declared approximation was not locally contained. constant/thermoPhysPropDict authorises hydrogen to run at gamma = 1, by name and with its reason: no UNIFAC group for hydrogen exists, and inventing one would be fabrication. The stated stake was small --- a liquid mole fraction of 2e-4. Three units downstream that residue diverges the rigorous MESH in C1, which is why there is a vent flash in this flowsheet that is not in his Figure 1. It is an explicit unit, not a deletion, so what leaves with the hydrogen is computed: the golden pins vent V\_over\_F at 0.00201400452928. This is the clearest thing the plant has to teach. 4. The tear seed is a guess, and the plant walks away from it. 0/ here is authored and committed, one file per stream, and 0/ipaRecycle is seeded with Luyben's own published recycle composition --- 3.822 kmol/h isopropanol, 0.004116 acetone, 2.053884 water in 5.88 kmol/h, which is x 0.650 and 0.0007 exactly as his table reports. The converged answer is x 0.4991. The seed is the author's, visible, and owned; the solver moved off it and said so. (Where a case ships no 0/, bin/choupo-init0 materialises one from the authored inlets and the tear seed.) 5. A specification that survives a recycle is not the same as a rate. C1 asks for distillateRecovery \{ component acetone; fraction 0.97; \} rather than Luyben's 32.25 kmol/h, because the acetone reaching C1 shrinks on every turn of the loop: a rate that is feasible on the first pass is infeasible on the third, and the flowsheet would then fail on arithmetic instead of physics. The golden confirms the spec was met --- C1 recovery\_acetone 0.969999992418 --- in three outer searches. C2 keeps his rate, because its feed is not starved the same way. 6. The plant still closes. Global mass closure at 100 \%, and the plant-boundary first law pinned at H\_feeds\_kW -5862.58875482, Q\_boundary\_kW 632.174396749, H\_products\_kW -5236.98782168, a residual of 6.57346360643 kW. A disagreement with a paper and a violation of conservation are different things, and this case is careful to be only the first.}
\tutreadme{Read the case's own CLAUDE.md first: it carries the full comparison against Luyben's Figure 1, the five traced sources of error, and a $\ast$Pending$\ast$ list that names the one change which would move every row --- fitted UNIQUAC or NRTL pairs for the three binaries, which is the honest way to close the gap and is a curation job rather than a code job. The build history is docs/design/acetone-plant-closure-state.md; the programme is docs/design/acetone-ipa-reference-case.md.}

\tutwhat{Full-scale ammonia SYNTHESIS LOOP at 200 bar (\textasciitilde{}59 t/h NH3, 1400 t/day) -- a synthesis-loop fundamental, not a whole ammonia plant: the syngas arrives as a declared 25 bar makeup and its production is not modelled. Explicit syngas + recycle COMPRESSORS, feed-effluent HEAT EXCHANGER, ADIABATIC converter (the reaction heats itself -- exothermic), water cooler + refrigerated separator, product let-down, and the recycle + purge. SRK fugacity throughout; dissolved H2/N2 by measured Henry constants (Wiebe 1934, Larson-Black 1925 via IUPAC SDS 5/6).}
\begin{tutnarrative}
the complete Haber-Bosch plant, \textasciitilde{}59 t/h NH3

makeup 25 bar  [makeupComp 25$\to$200]     recycle  [recycleComp]  [mixer]   mixed (cool)   cold side [FEHE]     hot effluent (heat recovery)   preheatedFeed (\textasciitilde{}683 K)   [converter] gibbsReactor mode ADIABATIC N2+3H2<$\to$2NH3 exothermic $\to$ self-heats to \textasciitilde{}840 K   hotEffluent   hot side of FEHE $\to$ cooledEffluent [waterCooler] (cooling water)   \textasciitilde{}310 K [separator] flash 250 K/200 bar (refrig.)     rawLiquid unreactedGas     [letdown] [purgeSplit]         productNH3 gas purge recycle     (tear)

THE REACTOR HEAT. N2+3H2$\to$2NH3 is EXOTHERMIC -- there is NO external reactor heating. The converter runs ADIABATIC: the exotherm raises the gas T (feed 683 K in, 840 K out), and the feed-effluent exchanger (FEHE) recovers that heat to preheat the incoming feed to catalyst light-off. Self-sustaining once lit. The compressors set the 200-bar synthesis pressure; the water cooler (cooling-water utility) + refrigerated flash condense the NH3. Every machine is explicit and its duty/work is reported.

CAPACITY \textasciitilde{}59 t/h NH3 (\textasciitilde{}1400 t/day) at 98.6\% product purity -- a world-scale single train.

DISSOLVED GASES BY HENRY'S LAW. H2 and N2 are supercritical at the separator (no physical Psat), so their dissolved amounts follow MEASURED Henry constants (pairs H2-NH3 from Wiebe 1934, N2-NH3 from Larson \& Black 1925 as evaluated in IUPAC SDS Vol 5/6), with the SRK vapour fugacity at 200 bar: K = H(T)/(phi\_V P). The raw liquid carries \textasciitilde{}0.5\% H2 + 0.2\% N2 -- physical, vs the \textasciitilde{}13\% a Psat extrapolated above Tc used to fake. KNOWN RESIDUAL: Ar has no measured Ar-NH3 Henry pair yet, so its dissolved \textasciitilde{}1\% is a Raoult-extrapolation artefact (\textasciitilde{}7x over by analogy with N2) -- the product's main impurity is overstated.

THE SIMULATION STRATEGY (how you build a plant like this). 1. PICK THE THERMO BY THE PHYSICS, per phase ("the two worlds"): the 200-bar GAS side needs real-gas fugacity $\to$ a cubic EoS (SRK) declared once in the package; the reactor folds phi into its equilibrium automatically. The DISSOLVED gases are supercritical solutes in a condensable solvent $\to$ the unsymmetric convention (Henry / Krichevsky-Kasarnovsky), NOT Raoult: pair files H2-NH3 + N2-NH3 fitted to measured solubility, `solvent NH3;` in the package, `role solute;` overlays on H2/N2 in this case's constant/. 2. TEAR THE LOOP WHERE INFORMATION FLOWS BACKWARD: one MASS tear (recycle, guessed then Newton-converged) and one ENERGY tear (hotEffluent -- the FEHE preheats the feed with the reactor's own product heat, so the converter's outlet is needed upstream of the converter). Both declared in solverDict tearStreams; the solver announces every iteration. 3. LET THE EXOTHERM DO THE HEATING: the converter is ADIABATIC (mode adiabatic; T is a guess, not a spec) -- the reaction self-heats 683 $\to$ 840 K and the FEHE recycles that heat to light off the feed. No phantom reactor heater exists anywhere. 4. MAKE EVERY MACHINE EXPLICIT so it can be SIZED AND COSTED: compressors by shaft power, exchangers by area, the converter + drums by vessel design bases (space velocity / residence time) in system/postDict $\to$ Turton costs $\to$ the DCF economics in constant/economics. Every unit operation carries its own sizing -- the doctrine. 5. VALIDATE AGAINST MEASUREMENT AT EVERY JOINT: the reactor equilibrium against the ideal-vs-SRK shift (gibbs10), the dissolved gas against Wiebe 1934 / Larson-Black 1925 (x\_H2 at 400 atm: 0.0287 computed vs 0.0282 measured), the balances against 100\% element closure.

HONEST SIMPLIFICATIONS. (1) The converter is a SINGLE adiabatic bed, so it runs hotter (\textasciitilde{}567 C) than a real multi-bed converter with interbed quench cooling (which stays near the 400-500 C equilibrium sweet spot for more NH3 per pass). (2) The makeup compressor is one stage (real: multi-stage with intercooling), so its discharge is hot. (3) The let-down gas and the loop pressure drops are as in ammonia01. (4) `water` is in the package ONLY as the cooling-water utility fluid (it is not a reaction species).

\end{tutnarrative}

\tutwhat{Ammonia synthesis loop with a THREE-BED QUENCH CONVERTER: cold feed gas is taken off upstream of the feed-effluent exchanger and injected between adiabatic catalyst beds, so the gas zigzags about the locus of maximum rate instead of riding one adiabatic line to a single hot equilibrium. Same loop as ammonia02 (200 bar, 3:1 makeup, 3\% purge, Henry-law dissolved gases); the converter is the redesign. The quench split is the design variable.}
\begin{tutnarrative}
the SAME synthesis loop as ammonia02, with the converter redesigned as THREE ADIABATIC BEDS WITH COLD-SHOT QUENCH.

makeup 25 bar  [T101] [makeupComp 25$\to$245]     recycle  [recycleComp]  [mixer]   mixed (26645 kmol/h, 386 K)   [quenchSplit] <-- THE DESIGN VARIABLE 47 \%  25 \%  28 \%  toFEHE  quench1  quench2        [FEHE]     hotEffluent (heat recovery)   preheatedFeed 683 K         [bed1]   841 K   [quench1Mix]        (682 K)   bed2Feed   [bed2]   798 K   [quench2Mix]          (681 K)   bed3Feed   [bed3]   778 K    hotEffluent     [FEHE] hot side

[waterCooler]      [separator] 250 K / 200 bar     rawLiquid unreactedGas     [letdown] [purgeSplit]         productNH3 gas purge recycle (tear)

WHY QUENCH. N2 + 3 H2 <$\to$ 2 NH3 is EXOTHERMIC and REVERSIBLE. Exothermic means an adiabatic bed heats itself as it converts; reversible means the equilibrium it is climbing towards RETREATS as it heats. A single adiabatic bed therefore runs up one straight line in the (conversion, temperature) plane until it meets the equilibrium curve, and stops there -- ammonia02 stops at 839.6 K and 10.75 \% NH3. A quench converter cuts the bed into pieces and drops the gas back down the temperature axis between them, with cold loop gas taken off upstream of the interchanger. The gas ZIGZAGS: up the adiabatic line inside a bed, vertically down at each cold shot.

MEASURED, this run against ammonia02 (identical feed, pressure, purge and separator; only the converter and the interchanger differ):

converter exit 10.75 \% NH3 @ 839.6 K $\to$ 17.28 \% NH3 @ 777.5 K per-pass N2 conv. 17.84 \% $\to$ 28.80 \% loop circulation 40545 kmol/h $\to$ 26645 kmol/h recycle 32545 kmol/h $\to$ 18645 kmol/h purge (3 \% of recycle) 1006 kmol/h $\to$ 577 kmol/h product 3498.7 kmol/h $\to$ 3719.8 kmol/h (+6.3 \%)

The product gain is NOT the extra equilibrium conversion by itself: it is that a loop which converts more per pass recirculates less, so the 3 \% purge throws away 43 \% less hydrogen.

THE SPLIT IS THE DESIGN. 47 / 25 / 28 is not a given; it is chosen. With the interchanger fixed at 375 m2, lowering the FEHE branch sends a smaller stream through the same area and preheats bed 1 MORE while cooling beds 2 and 3; raising it does the opposite. 47 \% is the value at which all three beds enter within 2.6 K of each other, at the 683 K that ammonia02's own converter already uses as its light-off inlet. Read README.md for the measurements, including what a BAD split costs and why a fourth bed is not obviously worth building.

WHAT THIS MODEL DOES NOT CONTAIN -- read this before quoting any number. Every bed here is a `gibbsReactor`: it runs to FULL EQUILIBRIUM, which is the same as saying it is infinitely long. There is no rate law, no catalyst volume, no particle size and no approach to equilibrium anywhere in this case, so: no bed can be SIZED, and system/postDict declares all three so that the engine refuses them by name on every run; nothing here can tell a good injection POINT from a bad one. Measured: moving quench from 25/28 to 50/3 leaves the converter exit unchanged to five figures, because with the last bed at equilibrium the outlet depends only on the TOTAL cold shot, not on where it enters. That is an exact property of the model, not a numerical accident -- and it is exactly the question a real design has to answer.

THE CONSTRUCTION IS DYSON AND SIMON'S. The rate contours in the conversion-temperature plane, the locus of maximum rate descending as conversion rises, and a cold-shot trajectory drawn as a zigzag about it, are Figure 2 of D. C. Dyson and J. M. Simon, "A kinetic expression with diffusion correction for ammonia synthesis on industrial catalyst", Ind. Eng. Chem. Fundam. 7 (1968) 605-610. This case executes that picture with equilibrium beds; their rate law is what would put the locus on it.

UNCHANGED FROM ammonia02, deliberately: 200 bar synthesis, makeup 1980 kmol/h N2 + 5940 kmol/h H2 (exactly 3:1) + 80 kmol/h Ar, both compressors and their shaft powers, the water cooler, the 250 K / 200 bar refrigerated separator, the 20 bar let-down, the 3 \% purge, the two storage tanks, the declared cooling-water circuit, and the SRK + Henry thermophysical package with its cited N2-NH3 and H2-NH3 pairs.

CHANGED, and each change is a consequence of the converter: the INTERCHANGER falls from 1500 m2 to 375 m2. It carries 47 \% of the loop gas instead of 100 \%, from an effluent 62 K cooler. Its duty falls from 117.2 MW to 31.2 MW. the WATER COOLER takes 66.2 MW instead of 57.8 MW: 8.4 MW that the interchanger no longer recovers leaves through the cooling water instead. A real plant puts a waste-heat boiler on that effluent. This case does not add one -- that is a separate design act, and inventing it here would change two things at once. the recycle TOLERANCE is 1e-8 instead of 1e-5. At 1e-5 this loop's element balance closed only to 0.05 \%; three reactors on one tear leave more room for a loose tear to show. NOT changed and worth seeing: the recycle compressor still takes 4000 kW on a circulation 43 \% smaller, so it now discharges at 258 bar into a mixer that runs at 245. The circulator is oversized for the converter it feeds -- a real consequence of the redesign, left visible rather than tuned away.

\end{tutnarrative}
\tutreadme{The same synthesis loop as ammonia02\_full\_plant --- 200 bar, makeup 1980 kmol/h N$_2$ + 5940 kmol/h H$_2$ (exactly 3:1) + 80 kmol/h Ar, refrigerated separator at 250 K, 3 \% purge, SRK fugacity with measured N$_2$--NH$_3$ and H$_2$--NH$_3$ Henry pairs --- with one thing changed: the converter. ammonia02 has a single adiabatic bed. This case has three adiabatic beds with cold-shot quench between them, which is what the BASF account of Haber--Bosch describes when it says the reacting hot gas is cooled with a supply of cold gas $\ast$inside$\ast$ the reactor.}
\tutreadme{Ammonia synthesis is exothermic $\ast$and$\ast$ reversible, and those two facts pull in opposite directions.}
\tutreadme{$\ast$ Exothermic $\to$ an adiabatic bed heats itself as it converts. Its state moves up a straight line in the (conversion, temperature) plane: every mole of NH$_3$ formed buys a fixed number of degrees. $\ast$ Reversible $\to$ the equilibrium conversion falls as the temperature rises. The target retreats as you chase it.}
\tutreadme{Between them there is a locus of maximum rate: at any conversion there is one temperature where the forward and reverse rates are furthest apart, and that temperature descends as conversion rises. A single adiabatic bed crosses that locus early and then spends the rest of itself on the wrong side of it, running into a receding equilibrium.}
\tutreadme{A quench converter follows the locus instead --- in a staircase. Inside a bed the gas climbs its adiabatic line; at the cold shot it drops vertically (cold gas removes heat, and dilutes, but converts nothing). Up, down, up, down, up. That zigzag is the whole design.}
\tutreadme{The picture is Dyson and Simon's. The rate contours in the conversion--temperature plane, the descending locus of maximum rate, and a cold-shot trajectory drawn as a zigzag about it, are Figure 2 of D. C. Dyson and J. M. Simon, $\ast$A kinetic expression with diffusion correction for ammonia synthesis on industrial catalyst$\ast$, Ind. Eng. Chem. Fundam. 7 (1968) 605--610. This case executes that figure with equilibrium beds. Their rate law is what would put the contours on it; see ?6.}

\tutwhat{AMMONIA REACTOR-MODEL LADDER, rung 1 of 4 -- FIXED CONVERSION. The ammonia synthesis loop with a conversionReactor on a DECLARED single-pass conversion of 25 \% of the nitrogen. Claims a converged MATERIAL balance and nothing else: no reactor size, no equipment cost -- and NOT a converged heat balance, which this reactor cannot deliver against an SRK-priced stream (README section 4). Diff the flowsheetDict against ammoniaReactor02\_equilibrium and the only block that moves is the converter.}
\begin{tutnarrative}
THE AMMONIA REACTOR-MODEL LADDER -- flowsheet, SHARED BY RUNGS 1-3.

Everything in this file except the `converter` block is BYTE-IDENTICAL across ammoniaReactor01\_fixedConversion, ammoniaReactor02\_equilibrium and ammoniaReactor03\_equilibriumApproach. Diff two of them and the only thing that moves is the reactor model -- which is the whole point: one rung of the fidelity ladder at a time, and nothing else.

makeup (N2:H2 = 1:3 + 1 mol\% Ar) -+ v [mixer] <------- recycle <--------+ | | v | [converter] <-- THE ONLY | 700 K, 200 bar DIFFERENCE | v | [separator] isothermalFlash 250 K, 200 bar | | | | rawLiquid-+ +-- unreactedGas | | | | v [purgeSplit] splitter | [letdown] | | | flash 20 bar purge --+ +-- recycle ------------+ | | (5 \% bleed) (95 \%) productNH3+ +letdownGas

SCALE. The makeup is 8000 kmol/h (N2 1980, H2 5940, Ar 80), which is 1 mol\% argon and H2:N2 exactly 3.0. This is NOT the scale of tutorials/steady/flowsheets/ammonia01\_synthesis\_loop, whose structure this flowsheet copies: that case runs 1 kmol/h of makeup, and at that rate the converter's catalyst charge is about 2 litres -- below the lower bound of every vessel cost correlation the engine carries, so rung 3 could not honestly cost it. The flowsheet is linear in flow (the flash and the reactor are both intensive), so the scale-up changes no intensive answer; compare this case's converter y\_NH3 against ammonia01's own golden and they agree.

TOPOLOGY ONLY. Stream state lives on disk in 0/, one file per stream.

\end{tutnarrative}
\tutreadme{A DECLARED CONVERSION AND NOTHING ELSE. The reactor is a conversionReactor: it converts 25 \% of the inlet nitrogen because this case's dictionary says so, and it would do the same at any temperature and any pressure, whether or not equilibrium allows it. That is what a yield reactor $\ast$is$\ast$.}
\tutreadme{READ SECTION 4 BEFORE QUOTING ANY DUTY FROM THIS CASE. DEV.md's C8 entry gives this stage exactly one claim --- $\ast$"Claims a mass balance"$\ast$ --- and that wording is load-bearing rather than loose. This case cannot honestly claim a converged HEAT balance, and the reason is the engine rather than the stage: its first law is out by 2 278.14 kW. The engine announces it loudly on every run, and section 4 diagnoses it with a probe.}
\tutreadme{Three cases form a ladder of reactor fidelity over one unchanged ammonia synthesis loop. Between consecutive stages exactly one thing moves: the reactor model. Feed, pressure, components, property package, recycle plan, tear seed, separator, let-down and purge are byte-identical across all three.}
\tutreadme{Background: docs/design/how-a-process-design-is-staged.md, and DEV.md C8.}
\tutreadme{A converged MATERIAL balance over the whole loop, and the consequences of one declared number.}
\tutreadme{$\ast$ No reactor size. A declared conversion contains no length scale, no contact time and no catalyst. There is nothing here from which a volume follows. $\ast$ No cost --- and the reason is the METHODOLOGY, not squeamishness. This case carries no system/postDict. By METHODOLOGY, an estimate that has only a declared conversion to go on belongs to AACE 18R-97 Class 5 (the class itself is set by the standard's PRIMARY characteristic, the maturity of the project definition, which no reactor model decides -- methodology is a secondary one), whose methodology the standard states as $\ast$capacity factored, parametric models, judgment, or analogy$\ast$ --- the whole plant scaled from a reference plant, with no individual item sized at all. Choupo's costing chain is per-item Guthrie/Turton bare-module: equipment factored, which 18R-97 lists against Class 4, not Class 5. So the engine cannot produce the RIGHT KIND of cost at this stage. It could produce a $\ast$number$\ast$; the number would be a Class-4 answer wearing a Class-5 label. The class table is transcribed once, in src/postProcessing/EstimateClass.H --- read the bands there, never from prose. $\ast$ It does not claim the 25 \% is right. See section 5.}

The flowsheet is linear in flow (the flash and the reactor are both intensive), so the scale-up changes no intensive answer; compare this case's converter y\_NH3 against ammonia01's own golden and they agree.

\tutwhat{AMMONIA REACTOR-MODEL LADDER, rung 4 of 4 -- KINETIC SIZING: THE ENGINE SOLVES THE BED VOLUME. The same loop as rungs 1-3 with the converter as an ADIABATIC plug-flow catalyst bed on the Dyson \& Simon (1968) rate law, and the bed VOLUME computed by the engine: a DesignSpec solves V\_bed so the effluent is 5 K short of the rate law's own equilibrium (US 5,352,428's per-bed definition, the same source and value rung 3 imposed), with a preheater landing the loop gas at rung 3's 700 K by its own inverse solve. The volume the engine computes sits beside rung 3's space-velocity volume, and the per-pass conversion a single adiabatic bed can reach sits beside rung 3's isothermal 46.60 \% -- both gaps are the lesson.}
\begin{tutnarrative}
THE AMMONIA REACTOR-MODEL LADDER -- RUNG 4: THE KINETIC BED.

The same loop as rungs 1, 2 and 3 (`ammoniaReactor01\_fixedConversion`, `ammoniaReactor02\_equilibrium`, `ammoniaReactor03\_equilibriumApproach`): the makeup, the pressure, the components, the property package, the recycle plan and the tear seed are byte-identical. What moves is the CONVERTER: it is now an ADIABATIC plug-flow catalyst bed integrating the Dyson \& Simon (1968) rate law, and its volume is what the engine COMPUTES (system/outerDict).

TWO BLOCKS DIFFER FROM RUNG 3, NOT ONE, AND THE SECOND IS A CONSEQUENCE OF THE FIRST. Rung 3's `gibbsReactor` declares `T 700 K`: it IMPOSES the converter temperature, and the duty it reports silently includes heating the loop gas from the mixer's \textasciitilde{}274 K to 700 K. A kinetic bed cannot impose a temperature -- it integrates from the state it is fed -- so the preheat that rung 3 folded into the reactor's duty becomes a unit of its own here (`feedPreheat`), whose duty is a RESULT. Diff this file against rung 3's and that is what you will see: the converter block replaced, and one preheater inserted in front of it.

makeup (N2:H2 = 1:3 + 1 mol\% Ar) -+ v [mixer] <------- recycle <--------+ | | v | [feedPreheat] <-- NEW: lands the | | loop gas at | v 700 K, Q result | [converter] <-- THE CHANGE: | adiabatic pfr, Dyson \& Simon | V solved by (1968), V a | the outer driver RESULT | v | [separator] isothermalFlash 250 K, 200 bar | | | | rawLiquid-+ +-- unreactedGas | | | | v [purgeSplit] splitter | [letdown] | | | flash 20 bar purge --+ +-- recycle ------------+ | | (5 \% bleed) (95 \%) productNH3+ +letdownGas

WHY THE PREHEATER IS A `phaseChanger` AND NOT A `heater`, measured. The `heater` takes a DUTY and returns T\_out (docs/ai/unit-ops.md); a fixed duty in front of a kinetic bed inside a recycle is OPEN-LOOP UNSTABLE: a larger recycle is heated less, the colder bed converts less, the recycle grows again, and the loop runs away to extinction -- measured here with both recycle solvers (Newton: the letdown drum received an empty stream on a trial step; Wegstein: recycle 12 998 $\to$ 15 378 $\to$ 23 475 kmol/h in three passes while the bed inlet fell 697 $\to$ 597 $\to$ 480 K). That is real physics and it is why an industrial loop preheats through a feed-effluent exchanger with a temperature controller, never through a fixed-duty heater. The engine's unit that TAKES a target outlet temperature and RETURNS the duty is `phaseChanger \{ outletT \}` (a built-in inverse solve, announced as SELF-TARGET); the gas enters and leaves as superheated vapour, so the duty is entirely sensible (`Q\_latent\_kW 0`) and the unit's emergent role label ("boiler" for Q > 0 on the vapour side) is a label, not a claim that anything boils.

WHAT THE OUTER DRIVER SOLVES (system/outerDict, a 1 x 1 DesignSpec): \$V\_bed so that converter.approach\_K = 5 K (US 5,352,428's per-bed approach, the SAME source and value as rung 3's) The manipulated volume lives in `variables \{\}` below; the unit reads it through `\$V\_bed`. Nothing here types a volume.

WHY THE TARGET IS AN APPROACH AND NOT RUNG 3's 46.60 \% CONVERSION. Stage Rung 3's converter is ISOTHERMAL at 700 K. A single ADIABATIC bed heats itself as it converts, and ammonia equilibrium retreats as it heats, so the bed's conversion is capped where its adiabatic line meets the equilibrium curve -- far below what an isothermal converter at 700 K reaches. That cap is MEASURED in the README (a volume sweep), and it is why no volume of this bed can hit rung 3's number: the target would be unreachable, and a DesignSpec asked for it would diverge honestly. The reachable, sourced target is the one the patent states PER BED.

SCALE, TOPOLOGY, SEED: read rung 3's flowsheetDict; nothing about them moved. TOPOLOGY ONLY here -- stream state lives on disk in 0/.

\end{tutnarrative}
\tutreadme{THE FIRST BED VOLUME IN THIS CORPUS THAT THE ENGINE COMPUTED. The same ammonia synthesis loop as rungs 1, 2 and 3, with the converter as an adiabatic plug-flow catalyst bed integrating the Dyson \& Simon (1968) rate law, and the bed volume the answer of a designSpec rather than a number anybody typed. The rate law is WRITTEN in this case's constant/reactions --- kinetics \{ type expression; \}, every constant of Eqs 2, 6--8, 18 and 19 beside the formula that uses it, with its unit and its equation number (DEV.md 4c C67, 2026-10-12: the kinetics live in the case; until then the law was compiled into the engine). The engine compiles the formula once, checks its dimensions, prints it back as PARSED in the run log, and pfr integrates it. Read the props bench first (tutorials/props/kinetics/ammoniaRate01\_dyson\_simon), which writes the same law and adds the paper's Eq 39.}
\tutreadme{Background: docs/design/how-a-process-design-is-staged.md ?3.4, ?6 and ?7.3, and DEV.md C8.}
\tutreadme{Comments aside, the diff is exactly: a variables \{ V\_bed \} block, a feedPreheat unit inserted between the mixer and the converter, and the converter block (gibbsReactor with T 700 K; P 200 bar; temperatureApproach 5; and its species list $\to$ pfr with V\_R \$V\_bed; nSteps 400; thermalMode adiabatic; and reactions ( ammoniaSynthesis )). Makeup, pressure, components, sealed property package, separator, let-down, purge, recycle plan (system/solverDict) and the tear seed (0/recycle) are byte-identical to rung 3, comments included (0/makeup, 0/recycle and system/solverDict say "all four rungs" in all four cases). Rung 4 adds two files rung 3 has no counterpart for --- constant/reactions (the rate law selection) and system/outerDict (the DesignSpec) --- and carries a system/postDict of its own, which since 2026-09-26 runs on the DesignSpec's representative pass and sizes the converter as a pfr (?6).}
\tutreadme{Why the second block is a consequence of the first. Rung 3's gibbsReactor declares T 700 K: it IMPOSES the converter temperature, and the 3 287 kW duty it reports silently includes heating the loop gas from the mixer's 274 K to 700 K. A kinetic bed cannot impose a temperature --- it integrates from the state it is fed --- so the preheat rung 3 hid inside its reactor becomes a unit of its own here. It is a phaseChanger \{ outletT 700 K; \} (the engine's unit that TAKES a target outlet temperature and RETURNS the duty, a built-in inverse solve it announces as SELF-TARGET) and not a heater, and that choice was measured, not preferred:}
\tutreadme{$\ast$ A heater takes a DUTY and returns T\_out. A fixed duty in front of a kinetic bed inside a recycle is open-loop unstable: a larger recycle is heated less, the colder bed converts less, the recycle grows again. With the Wegstein recycle solver the loop ran away in three passes --- recycle 12 998 $\to$ 15 378 $\to$ 23 475 kmol/h while the bed inlet fell 697 $\to$ 597 $\to$ 532 $\to$ 480 K --- and with the Newton solver a trial step fed the let-down drum an empty stream and the run stopped. That is real physics, and it is why an industrial loop preheats through a feed-effluent exchanger under temperature control, never through a fixed-duty heater. $\ast$ The phaseChanger's emergent role label reads boiler (Q > 0 on the vapour side); the gas enters and leaves as superheated vapour and the duty is entirely sensible (Q\_latent\_kW 0). The Tsat 150 K it prints is the bracket centre of its inverse solve on a gas far above every critical temperature, not a claim about anything boiling.}
\tutreadme{The 700 K inlet is inherited from rung 3: it is the one thermal fact rung 3 states about its converter, and inheriting it keeps the ladder's rule --- one thing moves per rung --- as close as a kinetic bed allows. It was a declared assumption there and is one here.}

\tutwhat{Screening three production routes to ammonia on paper: overall stoichiometry, heat of reaction, the electrolysis floor and the synthesis equilibrium}
\begin{tutnarrative}
SCREENING THE PRODUCTION ROUTES TO AMMONIA, ON PAPER, BEFORE ANY FLOWSHEET EXISTS.

The first rung of the ammonia ladder: Douglas' input-output level, the stage at which a route is kept or dropped on its gross margin. Three production routes make the same product by the same synthesis step, N2 + 3 H2 $\to$ 2 NH3, and differ in where the hydrogen and the nitrogen come from. GREEN: water electrolysis, air separation, synthesis. GREY: steam reforming of methane, the water-gas shift, air in a secondary reformer, synthesis; the CO2 is emitted. BLUE: grey, with the process CO2 captured and stored. Grey and blue share one overall equation; blue differs only in what is done with the CO2, which no reaction can show. Each route is sized to make 2936 kmol/h of NH3 (1200.0 t/day, the PEQ base case's design rate) from 1468 kmol/h of N2.

The four route and heat units run at 298.15 K and 0.02 bar. That is the REFERENCE STATE, not a process condition: below the vapour pressure of water at 25 C every species is the ideal gas its formation datum is written for, and an ideal gas's enthalpy does not depend on pressure, so every heat below is a standard one, with water as vapour (the lower-heating-value basis). The same heats are NOT process duties: the utility allocation every steady run performs serves them with LP steam and chilled water at 25 C, and those rows are not a design.

WHAT THE ENGINE ANSWERS, unit by unit; none needs a rate law. `electrolytic` and `reforming` are conversion reactors at X = 1 on the green and the grey/blue overall equations: their feeds are the raw materials per kg of NH3, and dHrxn\_kJ\_per\_mol is the heat of reaction on the ideal-gas rung, per 2 mol NH3. `waterSplitting` is the electrolyser alone, H2O $\to$ H2 + 1/2 O2, on the route's 4404 kmol/h of water: its duty Q\_kW is the least power a thermoneutral electrolyser fed STEAM can be supplied with, the FLOOR under the green route's assumed electricity (an electrolyser fed liquid water must also pay the water's enthalpy of vaporisation, the higher-heating-value basis, so its floor is higher). `combustion`, CH4 + 2 O2 $\to$ CO2 + 2 H2O, has a dHrxn\_kJ\_per\_mol that IS the lower heating value of methane, which turns a reformer's fuel, declared in GJ, into kilograms of methane and CO2. `synthesis150` and `synthesis50` hold the shared step at equilibrium at 700 K and 150 or 50 bar: the single-pass ceiling. It is the same for every route, so it decides nothing between them; it says what the next rung must add, a recycle loop.

THE MARGINS ARE IN THE README, NOT IN THE ENGINE. A level-1 margin is arithmetic on these flows and a list of prices: product value minus raw materials per kg of NH3, then a SECOND margin after the energy each route needs (electricity, reformer fuel, CO2 compression and storage, a CO2 price), each an assumed specific consumption. The engine's economics pass prices ONE plant per run and needs costed equipment, so it cannot price three routes that have none; the README states every price (the three the PEQ base case declares, the rest author-set and labelled) and works the table from the numbers this run publishes.

\end{tutnarrative}
\tutreadme{The common entry to the ammonia cases. Before any flowsheet exists, three production routes to ammonia are compared on their input-output balance --- Douglas' first level --- and on the energy each one needs, so that only the routes worth a feasibility study go on to one.}
\tutreadme{Illustrated design stage: screening (FEL-1 in a three-stage numbering). No equipment exists yet, so nothing here is sized or costed.}
\tutreadme{The ammonia cases refine a simulation along two independent axes, and each case is named by its purpose on one of them. The project-stage axis follows one green-ammonia plant from screening to basic design: what the project must decide at each stage, and the detail that decision needs --- here the reactor model, the exchangers and the economics all move together. The reactor-model axis keeps one synthesis loop fixed and changes only the converter, from a declared conversion to a bed whose volume the engine solves. They are two ladders, not one: a project does not mature by swapping an equilibrium reactor for a kinetic one, and a kinetic reactor does not make a study a basic design. A stage column says "illustrated design stage" for the same reason: the AACE class of an estimate is set by how far the project is defined, never by the stage a case illustrates or by the model it runs, so where a case declares estimateClass it is the author's statement of maturity.}

\tutwhat{APALUTAMIDE 60 mg FILM-COATED TABLETS, a drug-product plant (the API is BOUGHT): an amorphous solid dispersion of apalutamide in HPMCAS spray-dried from acetone in a closed nitrogen loop (blower, heater, spray dryer, exhaust cooler, -10 C solvent condenser, purge and N2 make-up), the recovered acetone to a tank for QC and reuse; dry granulation (blending, roller compaction, milling, a screen with a fines recycle), final blend, tableting with rejects, film coating (an aqueous PVA coat sprayed on and its water dried off by hot air) and packaging. Steady state at the CAMPAIGN rate (12 800 tablets/h pressed); the operating hours are a declared stream factor. Blending, compaction, milling, screening, tableting and packaging are MASS-BALANCE PLACEHOLDERS (no equipment physics). Every number a group would change is an author-set assumption, said so where it is declared (README).}
\begin{tutnarrative}
a drug-product plant: apalutamide 60 mg film-coated tablets. The API is BOUGHT; everything else is made here (DEV.md 4c C97, phase A). A BASE CASE: it runs, it is NOT optimised, and every number a group would change is a plain key, said to be an assumption where it is declared. The README is the narrative; this file is the topology.

THE BASIS (README section 2): 12 800 tablets per hour PRESSED, the campaign rate, of a 580 mg core carrying 60 mg of apalutamide in 240 mg of a 1:3 apalutamide:HPMCAS spray-dried dispersion, with a 3 \% film coat. The operating hours are the economics' stream factor (system/postDict), so the plant is solved ONCE at its campaign rate (steady state) and the year is that rate times those hours.

SOLUTION AND SPRAY DRYING (the closed nitrogen loop) acetoneFeed $\to$ [acetoneTank] $\to$ acetoneToPrep --+ apiFeed (BOUGHT) -------------------------------+$\to$ [solutionPrep] $\to$ sprayFeed --+ hpmcasFeed -------------------------------------+ | v n2Makeup --+ [SD] sprayDryer +$\to$ [n2Mix] $\to$ [blower] $\to$ [gasHeater] $\to$ dryingGas ---------$\to$ | | gasRecycle-+ \textasciicircum{} 393 K asdPowder exhaustGas | | | | [exhaustCooler] 308 K (cooling water) | | | | [solventCondenser] 263 K (NH3 refrigeration) | | | | recoveredSolvent condenserGas | | | | [recoveredTank] [purgeSplit] $\to$ purgeGas (vent) | recoveredAcetone | +--------------------------------------------------------- gasRecycle (TEAR)

DRY GRANULATION, TABLETING, COATING, PACKAGING asdPowder + MCC + silicified MCC + croscarmellose + silica + MgSt $\to$ [blender] $\to$ intraBlend $\to$ [rollerCompactor] $\to$ ribbons $\to$ [mill] $\to$ milledGranules \textasciicircum{} | +---------- finesRecycle (TEAR) <--- [screen] $\to$ granules granules + croscarmellose + MgSt $\to$ [finalBlender] $\to$ finalBlend $\to$ [tabletPress] $\to$ tabletCores +$\to$ tabletRejects water + PVA + PEG + talc + TiO2 + iron oxide $\to$ [coatingSuspensionPrep] $\to$ coatingSuspension tabletCores + coatingSuspension $\to$ [coatingPan] $\to$ wetCoatedTablets coatingAirIn $\to$ [airHeater] 333 K $\to$ coatingAir wetCoatedTablets + coatingAir $\to$ [coatingDryer] $\to$ coatedTablets + coatingExhaust coatedTablets $\to$ [packagingLine] $\to$ packagedTablets

TWO RECYCLES, both declared in system/solverDict: the drying gas (gasRecycle) and the compactor fines (finesRecycle). The recovered acetone is NOT recycled in this base case: it goes to a tank, for QC and reuse -- the README says why, and closing that loop is a group's question.

WHAT IS A PLACEHOLDER. The blenders, the roller compactor, the mill, the screen, the tablet press and the packaging line are FLOW PRIMITIVES (a `mixer`, a `splitter`): they conserve mass and energy and model NOTHING of the machine -- no blend uniformity, no ribbon density, no particle-size reduction, no compaction force, no tablet hardness. Choupo has no such equipment model; none is invented here. The coating pan is TWO boxes, a `mixer` (the spray lands on the cores) and a `solidDryer` (the hot air takes the water off), which is the mass and energy balance of one machine.

\end{tutnarrative}
\tutreadme{A BASE CASE for a pharmaceutical-industry project group (DEV.md 4c C97, phase A). The plant makes film-coated tablets of apalutamide: the active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) is bought, everything else is made on site --- the spray-dried solid dispersion, the granules, the tablets, the coat and the packs. It runs (a few seconds from a cold start), it converges, its mass and energy balances close, and it is deliberately NOT optimised --- every number a group would change is a plain key, said to be an assumption where it is declared.}
\tutreadme{The case is sealed: everything it reads is in its own constant/.}
\tutreadme{Read section 3 before anything else. Half of this plant is physics Choupo computes (the spray dryer, the nitrogen loop, the solvent recovery, the coating dryer, the heat exchangers); the other half is a mass balance with no equipment model at all (blending, compaction, milling, screening, tableting, packaging). The two halves look alike in the stream table. They are not alike.}
\tutreadme{Where the group must look for what this case could not verify: the EMA European Public Assessment Report for the product (its assessment report; the quality part follows the CTD, and the manufacture of the finished product is module 3.2.P.3), the TGA AusPAR above in full, and the patents on the solid dispersion and its process. Replace each assumption with what you find, and cite it.}
\tutreadme{The raw-material flows in 0/ are these per-tablet masses times the campaign rate (each 0/ file says which). If you change the rate or the formula, every 0/<feed> file changes with it --- they do not follow each other.}
\tutreadme{The placeholders model NOTHING of the machine: no blend uniformity, no ribbon density or solid fraction, no particle-size reduction, no compaction force, no tablet hardness or dissolution, no coating uniformity. Choupo has no model of any of these machines and none was invented. The coating pan is drawn as TWO boxes --- a mixer where the spray lands on the cores, and a dryer where the hot air takes the water off --- which is the mass and energy balance of ONE machine.}

\tutentry{esterification2sector}{tutorials/plant/esterification2sector}
\tutwhat{Esterification plant -- two sectors (REACTION + SEPARATION) sharing components; per-sector constant/ data (S1 kinetics, S2 NRTL pair); ethanol-water pair inherited from the standard library}
\tutreadme{A two-sector plant that exists to prove one thing: data lives with the sector that owns it, and a whole-plant run finds it there.}
\tutreadme{Components are shared across the plant. The kinetics belong to REACTION and are never copied to the root. The ethylAcetate-water NRTL pair belongs to SEPARATION --- a $\ast$particular$\ast$ datum, fitted for this separation --- while ethanol-water walks up to the standard catalogue. Three levels of ownership, one run.}
\tutreadme{That perNode is the whole case. The sector's pair beat the standard library, and the log says so rather than leaving you to wonder which one it used.}
\tutreadme{Feed 100 kmol/h equimolar acetic acid + ethanol at 360 K. The CSTR (V\_R = 0.5 m$^3$) reaches 34.2 \% conversion --- a PLACEHOLDER number: the kinetics in sectors/REACTION/constant/reactions are still the pseudo-first-order stand-in, not the 2nd-order fit this case's own property evidence supports (see CLAUDE.md, "Pending"). The flash at 355 K, 1.013 bar splits the product into a vapour rich in ethyl acetate (bp 350 K) and ethanol, and a liquid rich in water and the unconverted acid. Mass closes exactly: 34.18 + 65.82 = 100.00 kmol/h.}
\tutreadme{This case shipped for weeks marked .known-broken, and it earned the mark twice over. Its flash carried P 1.01325; with no unit, which is 1.01 pascal --- a hard vacuum --- so the K-values exploded and everything went to the vapour. And it was never wired: the sectors existed as thermo regions with the connections commented out, awaiting a "curation phase" that never ended.}
\tutreadme{Fixing it surfaced two real engine bugs, both of the same shape --- data owned by a $\ast$sector$\ast$ was invisible from a whole-plant run:}

\tutentry{CONVERTER}{tutorials/plant/greenAmmonia03\_basicDesign/CONVERTER}
\begin{tutnarrative}
THE MULTIBED CONVERTER -- ONE SECTOR, ONE PRESSURE VESSEL (DEV.md 4c C69).

Three adiabatic catalyst beds with an interbed cooler after each of the first two. The flowsheet still computes FIVE blocks -- each bed and each cooler is a calculation of its own -- but they are built as ONE piece of equipment: the beds sit in a basket inside a single pressure shell, with the interbed exchange inside the same shell. That is a fact about the EQUIPMENT, so it is said where the equipment is sized: system/postDict's `converterShell` entry names this sector, stacks its members' geometries into one shell at the loop's design pressure, and the beds' own shells become internal baskets that are not priced twice.

WHERE THE ARRANGEMENT WAS READ (2026-10-12), and what was not: The M. W. Kellogg Company, "Ammonia synthesis converter", EP 0 254 936 A2 (1988), read on the EPO publication server: "the vertical converter is contained within cylindrical pressure shell 1", three axial-flow catalyst beds "within the cylindrical inner shell", and interbed cooling "supplied entirely by the single indirect heat exchanger" inside it -- ONE interbed exchanger, not two. Topsoe, "Ammonia converter baskets S-300" (product page, read): three catalyst beds, radial flow, a BASKET installed in a pressure shell, in one version with an integral feed-effluent exchanger after the third bed. The page does not describe its interbed exchangers. Neither source describes TWO interbed coolers raising steam, as these two do; that arrangement is the base case's, and the one-shell grouping is the sources' general construction applied to it.

The stream names are the plant's, unchanged: the sector's inlet is the FEHE's preheated feed, its outlet the hot effluent the FEHE cools.

\end{tutnarrative}

\subsection{polycaprolactonePlant}
\grouptheory{polycaprolactonePlant}
\clearpage
\tutentry{properties}{tutorials/plant/polycaprolactonePlant/properties}
\begin{tutscheme}
\begin{tikzpicture}[>={Stealth[length=2mm]}, every node/.style={font=\scriptsize}]
  \node[draw, rounded corners=2pt, align=center, minimum width=3.1cm, minimum height=0.8cm, fill=black!4] at (0.0,-0.0) {\textbf{pclRepeat\_Tg\_yang2020}\\[-1pt]{\tiny estimateComponent}};
\end{tikzpicture}
\end{tutscheme}
\tutwhat{Close the loop: ESTIMATE the PCL repeat-unit glass transition Tg by the Yang 2020 group-contribution scheme --- the plant gives Mn/PDI, this gives the physical property from the SAME repeat unit -[O-(CH2)5-CO]-}
\begin{tutnarrative}
pclProperties -- CLOSE THE LOOP: process $\to$ molar mass $\to$ physical property.

The plant (../) gave you the chain statistics from the KINETICS: Mn, Mw, PDI on the polycaprolactone it makes. Here you ESTIMATE the polymer's PHYSICAL PROPERTIES from the SAME repeat unit -[O-(CH2)5-CO]- by group contribution --- the bridge from "how big are the chains" to "how does the material behave".

TWO estimators, two properties, on the repeat unit pclRepeat (M0 = 114.14):

(A) Tg, the GLASS-TRANSITION temperature --- Yang 2020 (run below). Repeat unit -[O-(CH2)5-CO]- decomposes into Yang main-chain groups: O x1 : MW 16 Yg -14.718 CH2 x5 : MW 14 Yg 4.026 (each) CO x1 : MW 28 Yg 4.370

M0 = 16 + 5$\ast$14 + 28 = 114 g/mol (matches the reactor M0!) Yg(inf) = -14.718 + 5$\ast$4.026 + 4.370 = 9.782 (1e3 g.K/mol) Tg(inf) = 9.782e3 / 114 \textasciitilde{} 86 K (the additive estimate) (Measured PCL Tg \textasciitilde{} 213 K / -60 C; an additive main-chain scheme is weak for a flexible aliphatic polyester --- the model tells the truth about itself, which IS the lesson. See the console's per-cent error vs the anchor.)

(B) DENSITY --- Van Krevelen (Bondi Vw). NOT runnable on PCL with the shipped data: the Slice-1 Van Krevelen set ships only hydrocarbon + chloro groups (CH3 CH2 CH C ACH AC CHCl CH2Cl); it has NO ester -O- / -CO- group, so the repeat unit -[O-(CH2)5-CO]- cannot be decomposed. Running it would HARD- ERROR with "unknown polymer group 'O'" --- the estimator refuses to invent a value (no silent zero). The honest path: density needs the ester groups curated into data/standards/parameters/vanKrevelen.dat first. The worked Van Krevelen DENSITY example lives in tutorials/props/estimate/vanKrevelen01\_polystyrene\_density (a pure- hydrocarbon repeat unit the Slice-1 set CAN do).

This is the same M0 = 114.14 the reactor's polymer\{\} block used for Mn = M0/(1-p) --- one repeat-unit mass, two places (process AND property).

\end{tutnarrative}
\tutreadme{A choupoProps sub-case of [../](..) (the polycaprolactone plant). The plant gives you the chain statistics from the kinetics (Mn / Mw / PDI); here you estimate the polymer's physical property --- the glass transition Tg --- from the same repeat unit -[O-(CH2)5-CO]- (M0 = 114.14, the exact number the reactor used for Mn = M0/(1-p)).}
\tutreadme{$\ast$ Tg via Yang 2020 (CC-BY) --- runnable. Tg(inf) = 85.8 K; the console prints the -59.7 \% deviation from the measured \textasciitilde{}213 K (an honest limit of an additive scheme on a flexible aliphatic polyester). M0 = 114 is goldened (an exact mass-balance fact); Tg is shown but not goldened as validated physics. $\ast$ Density via Van Krevelen --- $\ast$not$\ast$ runnable on PCL with the shipped data (the Slice-1 group set has no ester -O-/-CO- group, so it would hard-error rather than invent a value). See the full explanation and the runnable hydrocarbon example linked from the parent [../README.md](../README.md).}
\tutreadme{The full teaching narrative lives in the parent README. See [system/propsDict](system/propsDict) for the exact group decomposition and the estimator invocation.}
\begin{tutgolden}
\goldrow{diag}{pclRepeat\_Tg\_yang2020}{M0\_g\_per\_mol}{114}
\goldrow{diag}{pclRepeat\_Tg\_yang2020}{Tg\_K}{85.81}
\goldrow{diag}{pclRepeat\_Tg\_yang2020}{YgSum\_1e3gKmol}{9.782}
\end{tutgolden}

\tutentry{sugarPlantEconomicsSweep}{tutorials/plant/sugarPlantEconomicsSweep}
\tutwhat{Sugar plant ECONOMICS SWEEP -- IRR / payback / NPV vs RawJuice sucrose content (Phase-2 SweepDriver post-chain differentiator)}
\begin{tutnarrative}
/ system/flowsheetDict (PLANT level -- COMPOSITE)

The flagship sugar plant (the ChemicalPlantTutorial flowsheet, reused verbatim -- sectors and units included), here driven by system/outerDict: a SweepDriver walks the RawJuice sucrose fraction and runs the FULL post chain (sizing $\to$ costing $\to$ economics, system/postDict) on every point, so IRR / NPV / payback vs feed quality come out as sweep responses.

A composite node: it has `children` (sub-flowsheets, here the sectors) and `connections` (the pipework between them). The same shape a sector uses to list its units -- one level up. This is the plant-and-sectors shape.

Naming convention (see docs/ai/case-layout.md): SECTORS in CAPS : CONCENTRATION, DRYING, FERMENTATION Units in PascalCase : Cryst, Evap1, Evap2 Streams in PascalCase : RawJuice, Magma, Powder, EvapVapour Components in lowercase : water, sucrose, N2

\end{tutnarrative}
\tutreadme{This is the flagship sugar plant (tutorials/plant/ChemicalPlantTutorial) driven by a SweepDriver instead of a single pass. It exists to show the one thing a single CAPEX number cannot: how the project economics move when a process variable changes.}
\tutreadme{The driver runs the FULL post-processing chain (sizing $\to$ costing $\to$ economics, in system/postDict) on every converged point, so economics.IRR, economics.paybackYears, economics.NPV, ? resolve as ordinary KPI look-ups (the Phase-2 SweepDriver post-chain wiring). The result lands in sweep\_results.csv.}
\tutreadme{Sweeping the RawJuice sucrose content 0.09 $\to$ 0.16 mol fraction walks the plant from sub-economic, through break-even, to clearly profitable:}
\tutreadme{(Measured 2026-10-06 from sweep\_results.csv, after the BD dryer's air was sized for the richest point -- the design basis is written in 0/MAIN/BdAir.)}
\tutreadme{Richer juice $\to$ more crystalline sugar per unit feed $\to$ more revenue against an almost-unchanged plant cost $\to$ the IRR climbs and the payback appears and shortens. The NPV crosses zero between 0.090 and 0.104.}
\tutreadme{Both use the same constant/economics prices (EU Sugar Market Observatory white sugar, ECB EUR/USD, $\ast$Chemical Engineering$\ast$ CEPCI, US statutory tax) and the same system/postDict cost chain --- only the run mode differs.}
